studies.title: He Taught The Quran
studies.meaning: The surah opens with a name and then a verb, with no subject repeated: the Merciful, taught the Quran, created the human being, taught him expression. Teaching is placed before creating, which the commentators discuss at length and generally read as ordering by importance rather than by time. Then the created order is laid out as a balance: sun and moon by reckoning, plants bowing, a scale set beneath the raised sky and a warning not to cheat it.
studies.historicalContext: Classified as Medinan in the tradition this collection follows, though the classical authorities differ and many place it in Mecca. A well-known report describes the surah being recited aloud to the Meccan leadership at the sanctuary early in the mission. Either way it belongs to a setting where the divine name it opens with was itself disputed, since some Arabs objected to that particular name.

keyTerms.note: A noun for making something distinct, covering speech, writing and the ability to separate one thing from another in thought. It is named as a taught thing, not as a natural property of being human.
The word repeats three times in three lines, moving from something set in the heavens to something held in a merchant's hand. The same term carries cosmic order and market honesty without changing.
From the root for counting and accounting. Applied to the sun and moon it names calculated motion, the thing that lets a person predict a season or a harvest, and it sits one line before the scale.
A plural with no singular in common use, naming gifts in general rather than any one gift. The refrain built on it asks about denial rather than gratitude, which is a sharper question.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Weights and measures were the nervous system of an Arabian market. A merchant carried his own stone weights, and a shaved weight was the easiest fraud there was and the hardest to prove. Disputes over a scale could set clans against each other. To move in three lines from the sun's orbit to a hand on a balance beam was to run the argument straight through the place where a listener's honesty was actually tested.
studies.didYouKnow: The question that closes this passage returns thirty-one times before the surah ends, more than any other repeated line in the Quran. Its pronoun is dual throughout, addressing two groups rather than one, and the surah names them a few ayat later as humans and jinn, each made from a different material.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The order of the opening is the argument. Mercy is named first, teaching second, and the human being third, so a person arrives into a world where the instruction already exists. Language is then given the same status as existence, both taught. The balance that follows joins physics and ethics in one word, which means honesty in trade is presented as continuous with the motion of the sun rather than as a separate department of life.

crossReferences.why: Records the objection to the very name this surah opens with, which is why the name stands alone as a first line.
Takes the warning about the balance down to a single practice, measuring generously when taking and short when giving.
Pairs creation with teaching in the same order, at the very beginning of the revelation.

studies.applyIt: Weigh something today that you usually estimate: your portion, your hour of work, the time you said you would arrive. Not to be strict with yourself. Just to see the gap between what you assumed and what is true. The surah runs a straight line from the sun's orbit to a hand on a scale, and your hand is the end of it.

studies.theme: Time and the Brevity of Life
studies.title: Everything Standing Is Going
studies.meaning: Ships are named first, and the word used describes them raised up like mountains on the water, a human achievement immediately assigned to God. Then a four-word ayah cancels everything standing on the earth. Scholars differ over what the pronoun refers to, most reading it as the earth mentioned earlier. What remains is named as the face of your Lord, and the two qualities attached to it are majesty and the giving of honour.
studies.historicalContext: From surah 55, classified as Medinan in the tradition this collection follows though the authorities differ. No specific occasion is reported for these ayat. They sit at the hinge of the surah, where a long list of gifts, sea and land and sun and grain, stops and the whole inventory is declared temporary before the description of the gardens begins. The refrain continues without interruption across the turn.

keyTerms.note: A passive participle from a verb meaning to bring into being and to raise. Used of ships it points at the masts standing above the hull, and it keeps the making in the passive, without a builder named.
An active participle, so the sense is present rather than future: everything on the earth is in the act of vanishing now. The grammar makes decay a current condition rather than a coming event.
The pair joins what overawes with what gives dignity to others. The second word is active, so the phrase does not only describe God's greatness; it names Him as the one who confers worth.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Arab traders knew ships from the Red Sea and the Gulf, where vessels crossed to Abyssinia and India, and from the coast the tall masts of an anchored fleet did look like a range of low hills. Ships were the largest things human beings built. They were also the most obviously fragile, since a storm returned the whole enterprise to planks within an hour.
studies.didYouKnow: The double title at the end of this passage appears in only one surah of the Quran, this one, where it occurs twice: here, and again as the very last words of the surah. The chapter opens with one divine name standing alone as its first ayah and closes with another, so the whole is framed by names.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage puts a limit around everything the surah has been listing. Gifts are real and are still gifts, but nothing in the inventory lasts, including the one receiving it. That is placed inside a chapter about mercy rather than about warning, so impermanence is presented as part of the same generosity. Naming what remains by a word for face rather than by an abstraction also keeps the survivor personal, which is the point being made.

crossReferences.why: States the same survival in almost the same words, closing another surah with the identical exception.
Places the same ships in a list of gifts, adding what people extract from the sea to eat and wear.
Gives the same permanence as four names rather than an image, placing God before and after everything.

studies.applyIt: Look at the oldest object you own and work out how long it will outlast you, roughly. A watch, a book, a house. Then do the same for something you are anxious about this week. The passage is not asking you to care less; it is asking you to be accurate about duration, which usually changes the size of a worry.

studies.title: The Reward Of Doing Well
studies.meaning: One question sits in the middle of the refrain and it is the only line here that is not description. Is the recompense for doing good anything other than good. The word is the same on both sides, so the sentence is close to a definition rather than a promise. Classical readers took it broadly, applying it between people as well as between God and the servant. Then a second pair of gardens is mentioned, beneath the first.
studies.historicalContext: From surah 55, whose placement the classical authorities dispute, some naming it Meccan and some Medinan. No specific occasion is reported for these ayat. They come near the end of a long passage describing gardens, and the question in the middle of them is one of the very few sentences in the surah that is not either a description or the refrain, which is why it stands out to a listener.

keyTerms.note: From a root for what is beautiful and fine. It names doing a thing well rather than merely doing it, and the tradition uses the same word for worship carried out as though one could see God.
A word from commerce and from law, used of settling an account either way. It is neutral about direction, so the same term covers reward and punishment, and here it is paired with itself.
A dual, and the surah has already described a pair before naming this second pair. Everything in this chapter arrives in twos, matching the dual address of the refrain to two kinds of creature.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A garden in Arabia meant an enclosure with a wall and a water source, and owning one was the ordinary picture of having arrived. Wealthy families near Taif kept walled orchards of grape and pomegranate that took generations to establish. To describe two of them, and then two more below, was to describe abundance in the exact units a listener used to measure it: not acreage, but how many walled gardens a man held.
studies.didYouKnow: This is the only surah in which a single sentence is repeated more than thirty times, and the placement is exact: the refrain never falls in the middle of a thought. Here it comes three times in five ayat, so the question about goodness and the mention of the second gardens each stand alone between two identical lines.
studies.theologicalSignificance: A recompense described with the same word as the act removes the usual asymmetry between what a person does and what they receive. It is not a bargain with an exchange rate. The classical reading extends the sentence past the hereafter into ordinary dealings, so it functions as a description of how the world is arranged rather than only as a promise about a garden. The mention of a further pair below also implies degrees rather than one undifferentiated reward.

crossReferences.why: Names the same quality as something enjoined, setting it one step above bare fairness in the same sentence.
Attaches divine love to the same quality, in a passage about spending rather than about reward.
Introduces the first pair of gardens this passage builds on, attaching them to awe rather than to achievement.

studies.applyIt: Do one thing well today that nobody will inspect. Wash the dish properly, finish the email you were going to leave half-written, put the tools back where they belong. The ayah names the quality of the doing rather than the doing itself, and quality is the part that only shows up when no one is checking.
